Is it true that an arbitrary subgroup of $GL_n(k)$ that intersects every conjugacy class is
parabolic?

Here $k$ is an arbitrary field and $n \geq 1$. A parabolic subgroup of $GL_n(k)$ is understood
to be the full stabilizer of a flag of subspaces of $k^n$. The flag may be empty, so that

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.38

by P. M. Neumann

b) Is it true that an arbitrary subgroup of $GL_n(k)$ that intersects every conjugacy
class is parabolic?

Here $k$ is an arbitrary field. A subgroup of $GL_n(k)$ is *parabolic* if it is the
stabilizer of a flag of subspaces of $k^n$, that is, a conjugate of a block upper
triangular subgroup; the stabilizer of the empty flag is $GL_n(k)$ itself. For a finite
field $k$ the answer is trivially positive by Jordan's theorem (a proper subgroup of a
finite group never meets every conjugacy class), so the content of the question lies in
infinite fields.

The second half of the notebook's part b), "How far is the same statement true for
subgroups of other groups of Lie type?", is not a yes/no question and is not formalized.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Matrix

namespace Kourovka.«6.38»

variable {k : Type*} [Field k] {n : ℕ}

/--
A subgroup $H$ of $GL_n(k)$ is *parabolic* if it is the stabilizer of a flag of subspaces
of $k^n$: there is a chain $\mathcal{F}$ of subspaces of $k^n$ (totally ordered by
inclusion) such that $H$ consists exactly of those $g \in GL_n(k)$ with $g W = W$ for
every $W \in \mathcal{F}$.

Since a chain of subspaces of the finite-dimensional space $k^n$ is finite, this is the
usual notion: parabolic subgroups are the conjugates of the block upper triangular
subgroups. The empty chain shows that $GL_n(k)$ itself is parabolic.
-/
def IsParabolic (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) k)) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝓕 : Set (Submodule k (Fin n → k)), IsChain (· ≤ ·) 𝓕 ∧
    ∀ g : GL (Fin n) k, g ∈ H ↔ ∀ W ∈ 𝓕, W.map (toLin' (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) k)) = W

/-- The whole group $GL_n(k)$ is parabolic (it is the stabilizer of the empty flag). -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isParabolic_top : IsParabolic (⊤ : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) k)) :=
  ⟨∅, by simp, fun g => by simp⟩

/--
Is it true that an arbitrary subgroup $H$ of $GL_n(k)$ that intersects every conjugacy
class of $GL_n(k)$ (that is, for every $g \in GL_n(k)$ some conjugate of $g$ lies in $H$)
is parabolic? Here $k$ ranges over all fields and $n$ over all positive integers (for
$n = 0$ the group $GL_0(k)$ is trivial and the question is vacuous).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.38».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (k : Type) [Field k] (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) k),
      (∀ g : GL (Fin n) k, ∃ h ∈ H, IsConj g h) → IsParabolic H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.38»

    IsChain (· ≤ ·) (↑flag : Set (Submodule k (Fin n → k))) ∧

        W.map (LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.toLinearEquiv
          (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.toLin g)).toLinearMap = W

$H \leq GL_n(k)$ that intersects every conjugacy class of $GL_n(k)$ is the
stabilizer of a flag of subspaces of $k^n$ (and hence parabolic)?

  sorry

The empty flag is allowed so that GL_n(k) itself is included among the parabolic subgroups, as required by the decomposition notes.

The standard action of a matrix in GL (Fin n) k on k^n is obtained through Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.toLin and LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.toLinearEquiv; stabilizing a subspace means its image under this linear equivalence equals itself.
The theorem quantifies over arbitrary fields, positive natural dimensions, and all subgroups. Intersection with every conjugacy class is expressed as ∀ g, ∃ h ∈ H, IsConj g h.

/-!
# Conjecture 6.38

by P. M. Neumann

b) Is it true that an arbitrary subgroup of $GL_n(k)$ that intersects every conjugacy class is
parabolic?

Here $k$ is a field, $n \geq 1$, and a subgroup $H \leq GL_n(k)$ intersects every conjugacy
class if every element of $GL_n(k)$ is conjugate to an element of $H$. A subgroup of $GL_n(k)$
is *parabolic* if it is the stabiliser of a flag of subspaces of $k^n$, i.e. it is conjugate to a
group of block upper-triangular matrices (with $GL_n(k)$ itself included, as the stabiliser of
the trivial flag $0 \subset k^n$).

For a finite field $k$ the answer is trivially positive: a proper subgroup of a finite group
never meets every conjugacy class (Jordan), so $H = GL_n(k)$. The content of the question lies
in infinite fields.

The notebook also asks how far the same statement holds for subgroups of other groups of Lie
type; this part has no precise statement and is not formalised here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Matrix

namespace Kourovka.«6.38»

variable {k : Type*} [Field k] {n : ℕ}

/--
A subgroup $H$ of $GL_n(k)$ is *parabolic* if it is the stabiliser of a flag of subspaces of
$k^n$: there is a chain $\mathcal{F}$ of subspaces of $k^n$ (totally ordered by inclusion) such
that
$$H = \{g \in GL_n(k) \mid g W = W \text{ for all } W \in \mathcal{F}\}.$$
Equivalently, $H$ is conjugate to the group of block upper-triangular matrices for some
partition of $n$. The group $GL_n(k)$ itself is parabolic (take $\mathcal{F}$ empty, or the
trivial flag $0 \subset k^n$).
-/
def IsParabolic (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) k)) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝓕 : Set (Submodule k (Fin n → k)), IsChain (· ≤ ·) 𝓕 ∧
    ∀ g : GL (Fin n) k, g ∈ H ↔ ∀ W ∈ 𝓕, W.map (mulVecLin (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) k)) = W

/-- The whole group $GL_n(k)$ is parabolic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isParabolic_top : IsParabolic (⊤ : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) k)) :=
  ⟨∅, IsChain.empty, fun _ => by simp⟩

/--
Is it true that an arbitrary subgroup of $GL_n(k)$ that intersects every conjugacy class is
parabolic?

Here $k$ is an arbitrary field, $n \geq 1$, and $H$ intersects every conjugacy class of
$GL_n(k)$ if every $g \in GL_n(k)$ is conjugate to some $h \in H$. Parabolic means that $H$
is the stabiliser of a flag of subspaces of $k^n$ (see `IsParabolic`).
-/

    ∀ (k : Type) [Field k] (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) k),
      (∀ g : GL (Fin n) k, ∃ h ∈ H, IsConj g h) → IsParabolic H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.38»
